pr_title: Handle all exceptions in data nodes can match
pr_body:
During the can match phase, prior to the query phase, we may have exceptions that are returned back to the coordinating node, handled gracefully as if the shard returned canMatch=true.

During the query phase, we perform an additional rewrite and can match phase to eventually shortcut the query phase for the shard. That needs to handle exceptions as well. Currently, an exception there causes shard failures, while we should rather go ahead and execute the query on the shard.

The issue is addressed by folding the exception handling in SearchService#canMatch, rather than leaving it to its consumers. There isn't a single usecase where a failure on can match does not translate to canMatch=true (besides the bug that this fix is addressing). This has the nice benefit that data nodes will stop sending back exceptions for the coordinator to handle, which is unnecessary given that the handling is always the same.

Closes #104994

issue_context.title: Unsupported Operation Exception querying Frozen Tier data
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.12.0

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

Elastic Cloud

### Problem Description

I have an ILM policy with 10 days hot, 80 days frozen. Getting partial results for certain queries. Bounding the query with a date range filter to just hot data produces no errors.




### Steps to Reproduce

For context, an excerpt of the mapping:
```
{
    "dynamic" : "strict",
    "properties" : {
      "@timestamp" : {
        "type" : "date",
        "format" : "date_optional_time||epoch_millis"
      },
      "request_id" : {
        "type" : "keyword",
        "index" : true
      },
      "customer_id" : {
        "type" : "keyword",
        "index" : true
      },
      "ip_address" : {
        "type" : "ip",
        "index" : true
      },
...
}
```

If I do an non-time bounded query, as simple as the following, I get partial results:

```
GET /<my-data-stream>/_search
{
    "query": {
        "bool": {
            "filter": [
                {
                    "term": {
                        "customer_id": {
                            "value": "some_value"
                        }
                    }
                },
                {
                    "term": {
                        "ip_address": {
                            "value": "10.0.0.0/32"
                        }
                    }
                }
            ]
        }
    },
    "size": 5,
    "sort": [
        {
            "request_id": {
                "order": "desc"
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

The response metadata shows:
```
    "total": 114,
    "successful": 92,
    "skipped": 0,
    "failed": 22,
```

And the failed section shows many of these for difference partial indices that are in the frozen tier (excerpt):
```
      {
        "shard": 0,
        "index": "partial-.<index-name>-2024.01.19-000006",
        "node": "<node>",
        "reason": {
          "type": "unsupported_operation_exception",
          "reason": "unsupported_operation_exception: null"
        }
      },
```

This looks to be a limitation around querying the frozen tier that has been around for a long time. It is triggered by sorting on a keyword field, in that we try to retrieve min and max values for the keyword field but that is not supported in the frozen tier, as that's only supported for fields indexed with points (numerics and dates). I guess the least we could do is see how we can throw a more user friendly error, as well as document the limitation if we haven't yet.

> Is there any scenario you have in mind where sorting on a keyword field works against data in frozen tier?

The point is that "frozen tier" in 8.x doesn't involve `FreezeIndexAction`. That's for the old-style frozen indices feature that we deprecated in 7.14 and removed from the external API in 8.0 (the internal API remains, for testing purposes only). So whatever is happening in this cluster is not the same as what is happening in that test case.

Got it, thanks for explaining. Despite the action to freeze is different, is `RewriteCachingDirectoryReader` the same implementation as it previously was? What happens here is that the can match phase fails because it is not supported to get terms statistics, only fields indexed with points support that.

Ok I see, we are using the same `FrozenEngine` for partially-mounted searchable snapshots, so this should reproduce in a more realistic fashion in `org.elasticsearch.xpack.searchablesnapshots.SearchableSnapshotsIntegTests` too.

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bb016bdbe9b3db79d54a25c1aea5e5c9b4ed7260/x-pack/plugin/searchable-snapshots/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/searchablesnapshots/SearchableSnapshots.java#L452-L465

> That can easily turn into a very expensive operation, depending on how much data you have in the frozen tier. Ideally, you'd have a time range filter that allows to skip all shards that can't possibly match it without querying them, and not sort by keyword as primary sort.

Yeah, in our use-case we are also filtering on date ranges in all queries, though we'd still wish to sort by this keyword the same in our hot and frozen data. We can work around this however in this circumstance.

Thanks for your feedback: what I meant to highlight is that you need to disable the can match phase to be able to sort by keyword on frozen, and that disables all the optimizations around shard skipping that are normally applied when you provide a time range filter.

Ah I think I follow now, so if we set `pre_filter_shard_size` and used a specific date range filter, we could sort by keyword and potentially be OK (with the caveat that if the date range is large then we'd still query many indices)?
Yes, the query should work then but all shards that match the index pattern are going to have to execute the query.
Pinging @elastic/es-search-foundations (Team:Search Foundations)

Having spent more time on this, I apologize because the suggestion around `pre_filter_shard_size` was incorrect! Only removing the primary sort on a keyword would fix that. The core of the issue is that we are playing tricks to try and skip shards, but that should never cause failures. If there is an exception for any reason, we should always fallback to executing the query like we would without any skipping. I opened a PR to fix this at #117469 .
